problems.title: Arithmetic Basics
problems.statement:
Read two integers a and b and print the results of the five basic integer operations, one per line:
  1. the sum a + b
  2. the difference a − b
  3. the product a × b
  4. the quotient of a / b truncated toward zero (so −7 / 2 = −3)
  5. the remainder, defined as a − b × quotient (so it has the sign of a)
If b is 0, print undefined for both the quotient and the remainder.
problems.input: One line with two integers a and b, separated by a space.
problems.output: Five lines: sum, difference, product, quotient, remainder.
constraints: −10<sup>9</sup> ≤ a, b ≤ 10<sup>9</sup> (the product can exceed 32 bits: use 64-bit integers)
hints: Languages disagree on integer division of negatives (Python floors, Java/C/JS-trunc truncate). Implement truncation explicitly if needed.
Use a 64-bit type (long / long long / BigInt or Number in JS) for the product.

examples.explanation: −3.5 truncates toward zero to −3; the remainder is −7 − 2 × (−3) = −1.

problems.title: Leap Years
problems.statement: In the Gregorian calendar, a year is a leap year if it is divisible by 4, except years divisible by 100, which are leap years only if they are also divisible by 400. For each given year print YES if it is a leap year, otherwise NO.
problems.input: The first line contains q, the number of years. The next line contains q years separated by spaces.
problems.output: q lines, each YES or NO.

examples.explanation: 1900 is divisible by 100 but not by 400, so it is not a leap year; 2000 is.

problems.title: Event Bus (Observer Pattern)
problems.statement: Build an event bus where subscribers register for topics, and publishing to a topic notifies them in subscription order. The special topic * receives every event; a subscriber registered both to a topic and to * is notified only once (in its position in the topic's list). Commands: SUBSCRIBE name topic, UNSUBSCRIBE name topic, PUBLISH topic message words….

problems.output: SUBSCRIBED name topic / ERROR already subscribed; UNSUBSCRIBED name topic / ERROR not subscribed. PUBLISH prints PUBLISHED topic to N followed by N lines ␣␣name <- topic: message (two leading spaces): first the topic's subscribers, then the * subscribers not already notified.

problems.title: Custom Iterators
problems.statement:
Write your own iterator classes (implementing your language's iterator protocol: Iterable/Iterator, __iter__/__next__, [Symbol.iterator], C++ iterators, …) without building full lists first:
